findings.interaction: When #[authorize_once] is combined with #[initializer] and contract deployed with zero deployer
findings.issue: authorize_once provides no additional access control when deployer is zero. The check order is: (1) assert_initialization_matches_address_preimage_private (allows anyone if deployer==0), then (2) authorize_once_check. If caller sets from=msg_sender (themselves), the check passes with nonce=0.
findings.evidence: private.nr:176-185 shows check order. When from==msg_sender, only nonce==0 is validated (helpers.nr:107-111). Caller controls both from and nonce parameters.
findings.fix: Document that authorize_once on initializers requires non-zero deployer for access control, or add explicit deployer check within authorize_once when is_fn_initializer

findings.interaction: Functions with #[noinitcheck] reading storage that is only set during initialization
findings.issue: Functions can be called before initialization completes, reading uninitialized (zero) values. Critical security checks (like owner == msg_sender) may pass unexpectedly if owner is zero.
findings.evidence: private.nr:97-101 shows init_check is skipped when fn_has_noinitcheck(f). No runtime protection for storage reads.
findings.fix: Framework should warn or error when #[noinitcheck] functions read storage fields that are only written in #[initializer]. Alternatively, provide assert_is_initialized_unsafe() for explicit opt-in.

findings.interaction: Public functions in contracts with initializers may be callable before initialization
findings.issue: assert_is_initialized_public uses nullifier_exists_unsafe which is documented as unsafe (F-239). Public functions may execute before the initialization nullifier is confirmed to exist.
findings.evidence: initialization_utils.nr:29-37: 'TODO(F-239) - this is currently unsafe, we cannot rely on the nullifier existing to determine that any public component of contract initialization has been complete.'
findings.fix: Track F-239 resolution. Consider adding framework-level warning when contracts have both #[initializer] and public functions that read initialized state.

findings.interaction: Functions with #[nophasecheck] performing operations that depend on specific phases
findings.issue: nophasecheck disables phase transition validation but doesn't prevent calling phase-dependent operations. Operations expecting revertible phase may be called in non-revertible phase or vice versa.
findings.evidence: private.nr:104-120: initial_phase_store and no_phase_change_check are both empty when fn_has_nophasecheck. No validation of which phase operations occur in.
findings.fix: Document which operations are phase-sensitive. Consider compile-time warnings for nophasecheck functions calling phase-dependent methods.

findings.interaction: Private function enqueuing public call with hide_msg_sender=true to an #[only_self] function
findings.issue: When hide_msg_sender is true, msg_sender is set to NULL_MSG_SENDER_CONTRACT_ADDRESS. An #[only_self] check will fail unexpectedly because msg_sender != this_address.
findings.evidence: private_context.nr:1601-1605: msg_sender is set to NULL_MSG_SENDER_CONTRACT_ADDRESS when hide_msg_sender is true. public.nr:67-73: only_self checks msg_sender() == self.address
findings.fix: Document interaction. Consider compile-time or runtime warning when enqueueing to #[only_self] functions with hide_msg_sender.

findings.interaction: External contracts inserting notes into another contract's PrivateSet
findings.issue: Anyone can insert notes into a PrivateSet. The owner of the PrivateSet (not the inserter) becomes the owner who can nullify. Inserter loses control of inserted value/notes.
findings.evidence: private_set.nr:87-91 documents this: 'other people can insert notes into the set' but 'owner is still the only person with ability to remove notes'
findings.fix: Framework should provide clear documentation/patterns for when external insertion is intended vs when it's a footgun. Consider PrivateSetRestricted that only allows owner to insert.

findings.interaction: View functions reading notes create read requests as side effects
findings.issue: The #[view] check only validates is_static_call flag. Note reads push to note_hash_read_requests which is a side effect. In static calls, these side effects may still be recorded.
findings.evidence: private.nr:78-85 shows view_check only checks is_static_call. private_context.nr:183 shows note_hash_read_requests are tracked. Static call enforcement at kernel level needs verification.
findings.fix: Verify kernel properly handles/discards read requests from static calls. Document that view functions can still generate read requests.

findings.interaction: AuthWit validation in nested call contexts
findings.issue: AuthWit nullifiers include on_behalf_of and inner_hash (caller, selector, args_hash). In nested calls, each call level has different msg_sender. AuthWit granted for outer call doesn't authorize inner calls.
findings.evidence: auth.nr:261-274: inner_hash computed from context.msg_sender(), context.selector(), args_hash. Each nested call has unique combination.
findings.fix: This is correct behavior but should be documented clearly. Users expecting transitive authorization need explicit nested authwit setup.

findings.issue: Framework allows multiple functions to have #[initializer]. The init nullifier is the contract address, so calling any initializer prevents all others. First caller wins.
findings.evidence: initialization_utils.nr:45-47: compute_unsiloed_contract_initialization_nullifier returns address.to_field() regardless of which initializer. private.nr allows multiple initializers at compile time.
findings.fix: Consider compile-time warning for multiple initializers, or document intended use cases (e.g., different initialization paths).

findings.interaction: Reordering storage struct fields between contract versions
findings.issue: Storage slots are assigned sequentially starting at 1 based on field order (storage.nr:34, slot=1, then slot+=storage_size). Reordering fields changes slot assignments, corrupting data.
findings.evidence: storage.nr:34-81: 'let mut slot: u32 = 1' and 'slot += storage_size' show position-based assignment with no field name consideration.
findings.fix: Consider generating stable slot assignments based on field names (e.g., hash(contract_name, field_name)) or add tooling to detect storage layout changes.

recommendations: Add compile-time validation for dangerous attribute combinations
Track F-239 resolution for public initialization safety
Provide clearer documentation for feature interactions
Consider stable storage slot derivation based on field names
Add PrivateSetRestricted or similar for controlled insertion patterns
